chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Mismāʿ ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام:

That Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment concerning four men who testified against a man that they had seen him with a woman, having intercourse with her, so he was stoned; then one of them recanted.

He said: He is liable for one quarter of the diyah if he says, ‘It was made to seem so to me.’ If two recant and say, ‘It was made to seem so to us,’ they are liable for half of the diyah. If they all recant and say, ‘It was made to seem so to us,’ they are liable for the full diyah. But if they say, ‘We gave false testimony,’ they shall all be killed.

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: the prescribed blood-money compensation in a wrongful killing case
key_terms.رُبُعَ الدِّيَةِ: one quarter of the blood-money compensation
key_terms.شُبِّهَ عَلَيَّ: it appeared unclear or mistaken to me
key_terms.فَرُجِمَ: he was stoned as a legal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if witnesses in a zina case recant after their testimony led to execution?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal judgment of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning witnesses whose testimony led to a rajm punishment and who later recanted. It distinguishes between mistaken testimony and deliberate false testimony, assigning financial liability in the first case and capital punishment in the second.
